sources.name: NBA Stats draft history via the sportsdataverse hoopR mirror
NBA Stats draft history via the sportsdataverse hoopR mirror

credits: Win shares: Basketball-Reference (Justin Kubatko's method), read from CourtLens' full-history season totals.
RAPM: CourtLens' own 1Y fits (R01) after Rosenbaum and Sill; time-decay RAPM for rookies after Databallr's default.
DARKO Daily Plus-Minus by Kostya Medvedovsky (darko.app).
Draft lists 1966-95: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); 1996-2026: NBA Stats via sportsdataverse hoopR. Combine: NBA Draft Combine via hoopR.
Page reference: Databallr's Draftballr, refactored as Draft Classes; no prospect model.
caveats: Descriptive only. Value by pick averages what happened at each slot; it mixes team needs, traded picks, league size (10 to 30 teams) and changing draft rules.
Surplus measures the value a pick returned, not the quality of the decision: a pick can fall short for reasons nobody controlled. Len Bias (1986, pick 2) died two days after the draft.
NBA value only. Picks who played in the ABA, heavily in 1967 to 1976, are undervalued.
Win shares and minutes measure playing time and box-score production, not impact. RAPM covers only classes 2014 to 2022.
Classes 2023 to 2025 have fewer than four seasons: shown to date, never redrafted or scored.
Career value uses classes 1966 to 2005; players still active in 2025-26 count to date.
Rookie comparisons are early-season samples; under 100 minutes is flagged. Past rookies have no DARKO or RAPM at the same point, so ratings are shown, not compared.
